name: In Aid of the Myreque
aliases: In the aid of the myreque
start: Go to Canifis and down the ladder behind the pub there, through the secret wall and squeeze past the stalagmite on the east side of the cave. Speak to Veliaf Hurtz.
description:
After the attack on the Myreque by Vanstrom Klause and with the deaths of both Sani and Harold, Veliaf is counting on you to help. Now that the Myreque freedom fighters' base camp has been revealed, they'll need to move on and set up base somewhere else.

Veliaf has heard of a little known village south of Mort'ton, referred to as 'Burgh de Rott'. This could be just the place to set up operations to strike back against the evil of Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan and his Vampyric overlordship in Morytania. And who knows what other secrets about Morytania and its dark past will be revealed?
itemRequirements: A method to damage vampyres, either:
Efaritay's aid equipped in combination with any weapon OR
A blessed or regular silver sickle
A blessed axe (obtained during Animal Magnetism)
Silverlight (obtained during Demon Slayer), Darklight (obtained during Shadow of the Storm), Arclight, or Emberlight
1 piece of any food to enter Burgh de Rott for the first time
1-5 buckets (5 is 'highly recommended' to save time)
44 nails (42 are obtainable during the quest)
10 raw mackerel or 10 Snail meats (randomly chosen, but you can manipulate the choice)
On the standard spellbook for Lvl-1 Enchant:
Optional to give to Ivan Strom ('''Strongly recommended if you don't have a high combat level''' 85+, you will not get the items back):
15 stew (highest healing), salmon, snails, or slimy eels
recommendedItems: Combat 45
Fast travel to several locations
Myreque Hideout to start the quest plus 2 additional trips - fairy ring DLS, Kharyrll Teleport, Salve Graveyard Teleport, Slayer ring to Slayer Tower, or Fenkenstrain's Castle Teleport
Burgh de Rott (3 trips) - Mort'ton Teleport, Shades of Mort'ton minigame teleport, Barrows Teleport, or fairy ring bkr and take the swamp boaty
Any furnace (1 trip) - Amulet of glory to Edgeville, Ectophial, TzHaar Fight Pit minigame teleport, or fairy ring to Zanaris
Paterdomus Temple west of Canifis (1 trip) - fairy ring CKS, Salve Graveyard Teleport, Kharyrll Teleport, or Slayer ring to Slayer Tower
enemiesToDefeat: 2 Vampyre Juvinates (level 75) 'or' 4 level 50s depending on route taken
rewards: Access to the Temple Trekking minigame
The ability to make the Rod of Ivandis
The ability to hire Oarswoman Olga as a crewmate with Sailing 65
Completing this quest awards the player with 5 Kudos which can be claimed by talking to Historian Minas in the Varrock Museum
ironmanConcerns: *Obtaining 2 steel bars: **Smithing 30 to smith one from 2 coal and 1 iron ore **Completing Quest Daddy's Home rewards 5 steel bars **1/21.33 drop from black knights (Combat 33) **1/21.33 drop from moss giants (Combat 42) *Obtaining a mithril bar: **Smithing 50 (boostable) to smith one **1/21.33 drop from chaos dwarves (Combat 48) in the Taverley Dungeon *Obtaining steel equipment to give to Ivan Strom **The steel med helm, chainbody and platelegs can all be bought from Blair's Armour in Shayzien *Raw mackerel can be bought from Frankie's Fishing Emporium in Port Piscarilius. Note that you can reroll the random requirement to avoid needing to kill snails.
leagueRegion: <poem> Unlocking Morytania will auto-complete the quest </poem>

walkthrough.heading: Starting the quest
walkthrough.body: {{Main|Myreque Hideout}} {{Map|3495,3464|align=right|width=250|height=250|mtype=square|r=3|caption=The Myreque hideout can be accessed via the trapdoor behind the Canifis pub.}} Start the quest by speaking to Veliaf Hurtz in the Myreque hideout. To reach the caves where the hideout is located, you may either use fairy ring dls or descend through the trapdoor south of the Hair of the Dog tavern. If you used the trapdoor, search the wall south of the ladder and walk through the secret passage. If you used the fairy ring, head through two cave entrances to reach the secret passage. In the tunnel there is an eastern alcove, in the south eastern corner there is a hidden cave entrance - click on the wall to enter (you can rotate your camera to see the entrance). Talk to Veliaf. He will ask the player to travel to Burgh de Rott to establish a new base of operations for the Myreque now that their hideout has been compromised.

walkthrough.heading: Arrival at Burgh de Rott
walkthrough.body: 1 piece food you don't mind losing (required to enter Burgh de Rott for the first time) (bring additional if running past ghasts, or 1 piece of food with full druid pouches), a hammer, a pickaxe, a spade, 1-5 buckets, 6 planks, 44 nails. Keep at least 6 inventory spaces semi-free. If you have completed Shades of Mort'ton you can get the hammer and planks from the Mort'ton Razmire Builders Merchants builder shop. 'Note': You must bring the items required for this section with you to Burgh de Rott, as there is no functioning bank nearby until you repair it later in the quest. It is also highly recommended to have the rest of the items ready in your bank for the second stage of the quest. Head to Burgh de Rott, located south of Mor'ton to find angry residents at the gate. Talk to Florin from the outside of the gate and he will refuse to let you in, accusing the player of coming to steal their blood and food for the vampyres. Use your food item on the open chest directly in front of the gate, and Florin will then let you into the town. Shades will no longer attack you. Once inside, ask Florin whether there are any 'out of the way' places in Burgh de Rott, and he will suggest the cellar of the inn. First, you need to clear the rubble covering it.

walkthrough.heading: Clearing out the rubble from the bar basement
walkthrough.body: Go to the inn just south-east of the gate, climb over the broken wall, and mine the rubble covering the trapdoor by using your pickaxe on it. Open the trapdoor and climb down to enter the cellar. Inside are numerous piles of rubble. Mine the rubble, then remove it to place it in your bucket using the spade. If you forgot to bring a bucket, there is a bucket spawn near the well south of the front gate. Each bucket you have can contain 3 loads worth of rubble. Mine all of the rubble within the cellar. When the buckets are filled, climb the ladder and use them on the rubble pile just south-west outside the bar to empty them (the rubble cannot otherwise be disposed of). Warning: Any items you drop will disappear if you exit the basement. The rubble will reappear upon leaving the cellar and returning if you only mine it and do not remove it. 'Note': Every few rubble piles you mine, you will get 8 items: nails (10 bronze, 5 iron, 3 steel, 2 black, 1 mithril), 1 rock, 1 broken glass, dusty scroll, and plaster fragment. If you do not have space, they will drop to the floor, while the dusty scroll and plaster fragment will be discarded into the buckets of rubble, and can be reobtained by searching the rubble pile. You can read the scroll and fragment, but they are not needed to complete this quest. The rest of the items are not required for the quest, unless you do not have the required nails. When you have removed the final piece of rubble, a cutscene will play of you noticing a plaque on the wall. The plaque holds no significance for this quest. If the cutscene doesnt play, you need to return to the cellar and clear more rubble that magically appears. Go and talk to Razvan (who is typically located just north of the bar), and inform him that you'd like to help fix up the town. He will ask you to start by fixing up the general store. {{Clear|left}}

walkthrough.heading: Repairing the general store
walkthrough.body: Talk to Aurel in the general store in the north-eastern part of the city and also tell him that you want to help fix up the town. He will ask you to repair the roof and the walls of the shop. Head up the ladder on the outside of the southern wall of the General Store and use 3 planks and 12 nails in the hole in the roof to repair it. After that, head down and use 3 planks and 12 nails on the damaged wall just east of the ladder. :'Note': You can reroll the mackerel/snail meat requirement below by exiting Aurel's dialogue during the dialogue where Aurel tells you what he needs, but before he hands you the crate. Once done, talk to Aurel again and ask him what you should do now. He will want the store stocked before he can open it. He will always need 10 bronze axes and 3 tinderboxes, and will ask for either 10 mackerel 'or' 10 snail meats. You can provide him with either raw or cooked versions. You will be given a crate to fill up with these items. Visit a bank to retrieve the items and fill the crate with them. The items cannot be noted. While you are at the bank pick up these items for the next part of the quest: {{Checklist| *5 planks, *a hammer *swamp paste *20 nails }} Talk to Aurel again in the Burgh de Rott general store to give him the crate, and he will ask that you repair the bank to the south of the city.

walkthrough.heading: Repairing the bank
walkthrough.body: A hammer, 5 planks, swamp paste, 20 nails. Repair the bank booth by inspecting the bank booth, and then the wall on the west side of the bank as you did before. Then, ask Cornelius what to do next, and in the course of the conversation he will agree to become the banker. You will now be able to use the bank.

walkthrough.heading: Repairing the furnace
walkthrough.body: a hammer, 2 steel bars, 1 piece of coal, 1 tinderbox, food for lower levelled players, Efaritay's aid to use any combat weapon, or a silver weapon such as the Wolfbane dagger. If you cannot use Efaritay's aid and have access to other silver weaponry, it is recommended to use Darklight, Blessed Axe, or Silverlight in that order. Ask Razvan what you should do next, and he will suggest that you fix the furnace. It can be found in the south-east corner of Burgh de Rott. Take two steel bars, a tinderbox, a hammer and one coal and repair the furnace to the south-east side of the city. Inspect the broken furnace to repair it. Put the coal inside of the newly fixed furnace, and light it with the tinderbox. After lighting the furnace, you will see a cutscene. Vanstrom has noticed that Burgh De Rott is now inhabited and has ordered his blood tithe collector Gadderanks to collect blood from the residents. Prepare for a fight with your silver weapon 'or' any weapon wearing Efaritay's aid. Go to the general store, and talk to Gadderanks and then Wiskit. Talk to one of the Vampyre Juvinates and Gadderanks will order the two juvinates to attack you. They may be flinched by dragging them to the south of the room, then standing to the north of the table. You may also safespot them entirely from behind the table if using Ranged or Magic with Efaritay's aid. After one of the vampyres turns into mist, Veliaf will enter and assist you in killing the other vampyre, and then finally Gadderanks himself. 'Note': You may leave the room at any time, which will cause the fight to reset. {{bug|Occasionally, juvinates may not turn into mist and will instead become invincible. If this happens, leave the general store and try again. Switching to a non silver weapon for a few hits may also work.}} Once all three have been dispatched, talk to Gadderanks who will be lying on the floor. He will beg you to try and save his family, and in return offers you information of the vampre's weaknesses, before finally succumbing to his injuries. Aurel will pick up his Gadderhammer and give it to you (if you have no free inventory space, it can be claimed from him later). Talk to Veliaf, and he will tell you to meet him back at his hideout in the Hollows so the Myreque can discuss the move to Burgh de Rott. {{Clear}}

walkthrough.heading: Transporting Ivan
walkthrough.body: Armour, food, and a Efaritay's aid to use any combat weapon, or a silver weapon slimy eel]] as food. You will not get back any items you give to Ivan. 'Note': You will be prevented from bringing pets in the following section, so bank them now. Return to Veliaf in the Myreque Hideout and talk to him. He will ask you talk to Radigad and Polmafi to have them head to the Burgh de Rott hideout, but wants you to escort Ivan Strom to the Paterdomus Temple because the mission is becoming too dangerous for the young, aspiring priest. After escorting Ivan, he also wants you to ask Drezel about the rumours of a powerful weapon owned by a man named Ivandis Seergaze. {{Instance}} Talk to either Radigad Ponfit or Polmafi Ferdygris, and they will inform the other that it is time to leave. If you brought items for Ivan, right-click and "use" the items on him. Speak to Ivan when you're ready to escort him through the swamp. You will be asked to select between Route 1 (short route) and Route 2 (long route). The short route involves a fight against two level 75 Vampyre Juvinates, and the long route involves a fight against four level 50 Vampyre Juvinates. Although the short route is a harder fight, it is easier to defend Ivan from just two enemies, so choosing this route is recommended. If Ivan's health becomes too low, or he runs out of food, he will teleport out. He will let you know in the chat how much food he has remaining. If he teleports out, killing the juvinates will not progress the quest. You will need to leave the area to the south which will take you somewhere around Canifis so you can return to the hideout and try again. You will need to give him food again as he will have run out. If you leave the area while Ivan is still around, he will return to the hideout with the same amount of food that he had left. The easiest way to protect Ivan is to ensure that he stays behind you. If using melee, just attack the juvinate directly in front of you to occupy him. If using Ranged or Magic with Efaritay's Aid, don't move from the starting square to ensure that Ivan does not move at all, and also attack the juvinate directly in front of you. If using this method, the other juvinate/s will wander around for a while, and then eventually engage Ivan. Once you have killed the first vampyre, you can prevent the second vampyre from attacking Ivan by standing behind him, initiating a conversation with him, and then moving into the square where Ivan was. He will then move one square behind you, blocking the vampyre from attacking him. It is possible to finish either route without giving Ivan anything, but it is difficult, and it will often require several attempts just to keep Ivan alive. Therefore, it is highly recommended to give Ivan armour and food. {{Bug|There is a bug where it is possible to complete the trek without completing the instance. Just continue the quest as normal.}} After successfully escorting Ivan, climb down the trapdoor to the west and talk to Drezel. He will thank you for bringing Ivan; ask him where you might get more information on Ivandis's weapon, and he will give guarded answers. Tell him that the lives of those few left in Morytania rest on this, and he will relent and give you a key to the library. Use your key on the empty wall to the east containing a keyhole, and a trapdoor will appear. Go down the trapdoor into the library, and search the middle bookcase facing the western wall; you will pick up a book titled inside The sleeping seven. Read the book.

walkthrough.heading: The rod of Ivandis
walkthrough.body: Hammer, soft clay, mithril bar, silver bar, 1 water rune (or water staff) and 1 cosmic rune (make sure you have the normal spellbook activated for lvl-1 Enchant), a cut sapphire, and a rope. Return to the tunnel just outside the Myreque hideout, and just to the east of the northern brick wall you should see two wooden boards forming an 'X' which are covering an entrance - use a hammer on the boards and then enter the cave entrance that appears. Inside the cave is a coffin. Use some soft clay on the coffin to get a rod mould. 'Note': If 'nothing interesting happens', you forgot to read "The sleeping seven". Head to any furnace with your rod mould, and use a silver bar, mithril bar, and cut sapphire to craft a Silvthrill rod, and then enchant it using Lvl-1 Enchant. 'Note': If using fairy rings for travel, pick a location like the Edgeville furnace where you can quickly return to Canifis using CKS afterwards. Take the enchanted Silvthrill rod and a rope back to the basement of Paterdomus Temple, and use the rod on the well in the room next to Drezel with the rope in your inventory to create the Rod of ivandis(10). Take the Rod of ivandis to Burgh de Rott, go into the cellar of the pub, and give it to Veliaf to complete the quest. 'Congratulations, quest complete!'

steps: Climb down the trapdoor behind the Canifis pub.
Search the wall and enter the cave entrance just south-east.
Talk to Veliaf Hurtz.
Talk to Florin through the gate to Burgh de Rott.
Put a piece of food into the open chest, then open the gate.
Talk to Razvan near the pub.
Enter the pub, climb over the broken wall, then use your pickaxe on the rubble blocking the trapdoor.
Climb down and mine the rest of the rubble. 'Anything you drop in the basement will be lost upon leaving.'
Use your spade on the remnants to fill the buckets. There is enough here to fill five buckets.
Upon mining the rubble, you will find a plaster fragment and a dusty scroll.
The items dug up can be safely dropped, unless you need the nails.
When finished, use the buckets of rubble on the rubble pile outside the pub.
Talk to Razvan again.
Talk to Aurel in the general store to the north-east.
Climb up the ladder right outside.
Use 3 planks and 12 nails on the broken roof of the store.
Climb back down and Use 3 planks and 12 nails on the damaged wall of the general store.
Talk to Aurel again to get a crate.
'Tip:' If you are asked for items you aren't satisfied with 'before' receiving the crate, you can disrupt the dialogue by walking away to re-roll the requested items.
If you weren't able to bring all of the items, head to a bank now to get the remaining items for this section.
Add 10 bronze axes, 10 raw mackerels 'or' 10 snails (depending on what is asked), and 3 tinderboxes to the crate.
Talk to Aurel.
Talk to Cornelius in the bank.
Use a hammer with 2 planks, 1 swamp paste, and 8 nails on the broken bank booth
Use a hammer with 3 planks and 12 nails on the damaged wall outside.
Talk to Cornelius to recruit him.
Talk to Razvan.
Repair the furnace to the south-east. Use your steel bars, then coal, then tinderbox on the furnace.
Talk to Gadderanks in the general store.
Talk to the Vampyre Juvinate in the store.
Talk to Wiskit.
Kill the two juvinates and then Gadderanks (you'll need a silver weapon or Wolfbane dagger or Efaritay's aid to damage them).
Talk to Gadderanks.
Talk to Veliaf Hurtz.
Talk to Veliaf Hurtz in the hideout where the quest started. (The room under the Canifis pub)
Talk to Polmafi Ferdygris.

'Highly Recommended'''<nowiki/>: Give Ivan Strom some food (he only takes snail, salmon, slimy eel, or stew) and steel armour (he only takes a steel med helm, steel chainbody, and steel platelegs) before leaving.''
Talk to Ivan Strom to go on a simplified version of Temple Trekking and take either the short or long route. (you can't bring a pet - it must be banked!)
Route 1 features two level 75 Vampyre Juvinates, whereas route 2 features 4 level 50 Juvinates.
Kill the Vampyre Juvinates before they can kill Ivan Strom.
Tip: Alternate your attacks between them so they stay focused on you. Also, it may be possible to talk to Ivan to prevent the vampyre from attacking him
After you're done escorting Ivan, talk to Drezel in the underground temple for a key.
Use the key on the keyhole on the eastern wall and climb down the trapdoor.
Search the bookcases in the hidden room until you find The sleeping seven (The title of the book at the top when reading it is "The Sleeping Seven"). Read it.
Return to the room under the Canifis pub, then go to the blockaded cave entrance just south-east of the wall.
Use a hammer on the wooden boards and enter the cave.
Use your soft clay on the coffin to make a rod mould.
Go to any furnace with your mould, a silver bar, a mithril bar and a sapphire, and craft a silvthrill rod. (Fairy ring dkr for Edgeville Furnace.)
Cast Lvl-1 Enchant on the rod.
Use the rod on the well underneath the Paterdomus Temple (where Drezel was) with a rope in your inventory. (Nearest fairy ring cks)
Return to the Burgh de Rott pub basement with the Rod of Ivandis (it must be in your inventory, not equipped), then speak to Veliaf.
'Congratulations, quest complete!'

name: A Soul's Bane
start: Go east of Varrock, through the gate by the Earth Altar and just south of there, speak to Launa.
description: A rift in the ground has opened up releasing all manner of strange monsters into the lands near the Digsite. A sorrowful mother waits at the top of the rift for her long lost son, who has been missing for 25 years. You can journey down into the rift for an adventure full of twisted monsters all created from the mind of a young boy driven to madness through incarceration.
recommendedItems: Combat 30
Food
Digsite pendant or Digsite teleport
3-4 antidote++ or antipoison
Armour
A method of attacking with Ranged or Magic
A fast weapon, such as bronze darts
enemiesToDefeat: 7-8 angry unicorns, angry bears, angry giant rats, and/or angry goblins
6 confusion beasts (level 43) — must tank them, cannot kill
rewards: Access to Tolna's rift for combat training
requiredFor: Medium Varrock Diary - Enter the Tolna dungeon after completing the quest.
leagueRegion: <poem> Not completable, as it requires access to Misthalin. </poem>

walkthrough.heading: The missing family
walkthrough.body: Combat gear: Ranged or Magic is recommended for lower level players, as enemies only have melee offensive stats. Though some may attack at ranged, their damage will be less. Note that in the first room, you must use given melee weapons. Head east of Varrock, through the gate by the Earth Altar, and speak to Launa. The Digsite pendant teleport will place you slightly south-east of the entrance. Alternatively, take a glider to the Digsite. Launa explains that she is looking for her son, Tolna, as well as husband, who went down into the rift to find him. Offer to help her find them, then use a rope on the rift and climb down to start a cutscene. Be careful not to click during this cutscene or subsequent ones, else you'll teleport out and be forced to go through them again. {{Clear}}

walkthrough.heading: Tolna's rift
walkthrough.body:
{{Instance}} The rift contains four combat rooms, as well as a final boss room at the end. After completing a room, players may choose to leave the rift to get food or supplies, with their progress saved. Any incomplete rooms will be restarted, however. Logging out will also cause the player to leave the rift. Be aware that the entire quest is instanced. On death, all unprotected items will be moved to a grave outside the rift, and any items left on the ground will be lost. 'Do not drop anything' you'll need later on. ====Rage==== {{Cquote2|''"Why should I, Tolna, be trapped in such a wretched place? Arrghh, It's not fair! Feel my ANGER!"}} This room represents Tolna's anger by frustrating players, as they can only hit monsters with certain weapons.''
The rage room has four types of monsters, which must be killed to fill a rage meter. When entering this room, players will see a weapon rack, which contains four types of weapons. Each of the weapons only work on a specific monster, and will deal normal damage multiplied by 10 when correctly chosen.To defeat the monster, unwield your weapon and shield, and select one of the weapons from the rack and wield it. Only one weapon can be taken at a time. Once you have the weapon, kill the monster it can damage, based on the table below: {| class="wikitable" |+!Monster!Monster name!Weapon!Weapon name |- | |Angry unicorn | |Anger sword |- | |Angry bear | |Anger spear |- | |Angry giant rat | |Anger mace |- | |Angry goblin | |Anger battleaxe |} Players will do large amounts of damage on these creatures, but no experience will be gained. Each creature killed will fill the "rage level" bar at the top of the screen. After several kills of the player's choice of angry creatures, the bar will reach maximum and the player will yell, spin, and kill all remaining monsters in the room. This grants the player 40 Attack experience. A cutscene will then play, in which Tolna leaves his mother for a more lucrative life. Players can then exit out of the rage room near the east end of the cave, and proceed to the next room.
====Fear==== {{Cquote2|''"It's so quiet and dark. I FEAR I may never escape this horrid place. Mum, Dad, help me!"}}This room represents Tolna's fear, giving players a frightening jolt when they don't know whether or not a fear reaper will attack.''
In this room, you will find multiple dark holes lining the outer walls. One of these holes is too dark and frightening to search, while the others have a chance of triggering a 'jumpscare' and summoning a fear reaper. You will have to kill five of these in order to progress. Which hole that spawns a fear reaper is random and changes after each kill, requiring you to move around the room and search different holes after each encounter. Depending on your luck, you might need to circle the room up to five times to get defeat all five reapers. The creatures are large and only attack with melee, allowing them to be easily safespotted.
{| class="wikitable" |+After each kill your character is less afraid.!Kill count!Message |- |1 |I don't like looking in these holes but I must! |- |2 |I don't feel quite so afraid now. |- |3 |These holes aren't that spooky. |- |4 |This isn't so scary after all! |} After the final kill, your character will remark "Phew, I don't feel so scared now. This feels like the figment of someone's imagination!", and a cutscene will be triggered. Following the cutscene, the hole to the west will be lit up, and you will be able to proceed.
====Confusion==== {{Cquote2|"Where am I, How long have I been here? Am I still the person I once was? Oh why am I so CONFUSED?"}}''This room represents Tolna's confusion, flabbergasting the player because some doors lead nowhere and some beasts can't be hurt. '' {{Bug|If you don't see any monsters when you enter this room, simply log out and log back in.}} In this room, there are six confusing doors. There are also five confusion beasts, but only one of them is real at the time; the others are illusions, and cannot be damaged (although they will still grant combat experience). :'Tip': On the RuneLite client, it is possible to color each beast with external plugins. When you find the right one, that same color will be the correct beast all 6 times. The illusions will disappear after you hit eight zeroes on them; players can simply keep attacking the beasts until they disappear, or disengage by running to the opposite corner and then attacking another beast. Once you kill the real confusion, one of the confusing doors will vanish, and the rest of the beasts will respawn. Repeat the previous process four more times, until only one door remains, at which point a cutscene will trigger. Ranged or Magic is best for this step, as the beasts attack from a distance. When using melee, they have a chance to inflict poison, which can be negated by attacking with a long-distance weapon. Throwing knives, multi-hit weapons, or other fast weapons are helpful for speedy kills on the illusions. Illusions will chase you after attacking, and will keep you from attacking any of the other monsters while you are still in combat. You will see a cutscene after the last kill. After that, you can proceed through the final Confusing Door. ====Hopelessness==== {{Cquote2|''"What's the point? No-One will ever help me. I'm not worth anything, will anyone ever combat my HOPELESSNESS?"}} This room represents Tolna's hopelessness — players must not give up when the creatures reappear after dying.'' In this room are five hopeless creatures, which need to be killed three times each to fully die. Be careful of eating, as the monster's health will be restored. Additionally, if they are poisoned, the poison effect is lost when they reach their next phase. The creatures can use melee on their second and third forms, but will default to ranged after some time if they cannot reach the player. It is recommended to kill them from a distance as their ranged attacks are much weaker. Once they have all died, the Bridge of Hope will appear. After crossing the bridge, go through the exit, which will trigger a short cutscene. ====Tolna==== The final room contains Tolna, a three-headed beast which must be slain in order to revert him back to a human. The final room is a multicombat zone, and all three heads will attack at once. They use a ranged attack from a distance, and the northern head will very rapidly melee when up close. They are not very strong, but they attack quickly and can poison, so players should bring an antipoison and a decent amount of food. The three heads are very easy to beat with Ranged or Magic, although be warned that if using range without an accumulator, player will not be able to retrieve their arrows. After killing each head, Tolna will become human again. Talk to Tolna, and he will take you back to the surface. Talk to him again to finish the quest. 'Congratulations, quest complete!' :'Tip:' Re-enter the dungeon right after completing the quest to complete a medium Varrock Diary task.'' {{Clear}}

steps: From Varrock, head north-east towards the Digsite talk to Launa by the rift.
Enter the rift with your rope.
'Note': This will generate a cut scene. Do not click outside of the text boxes as you will return to the surface.
Use weapons from the rack to kill monsters until rage bar is full. '(Logging out will reset the rage bar)'
Anger sword - kills Angry unicorn.
Anger spear - kills Angry bear.
Anger mace - kills Angry giant rat.
Anger battleaxe - kills Angry goblin.
When your rage bar is full you'll get a cutscene '(this gives 40 Attack experience!)'.
Head east to the next cave.
Look inside the dark holes, some will have a fear reaper.
You cannot search the same hole repeatedly. Search the holes going clock-wise for as many rotations as it takes to get your kills.
Kill 5 or 6 reapers to get a cutscene.
Enter the black hole to the west.
Defeat confusion beasts until you find the one that takes damage. The "fake" ones give combat XP on missed hits and will vanish after 8 hits.
You can disengage a beast by running to the opposite end of the room.
If you're attacking a fake one, you can swap to a fast attacking weapon to kill it faster.
If you quickly swap after attacking one(darts/knife), you can check for 2 fakes and only have to hit one of them 8 times
Repeat until one door remains to get the cutscene.
Enter the remaining confusing door.
Kill all the hopeless creatures 3 times each.
Cross the bridge and prepare to fight Tolna (3 level-46 monsters).
Kill the 3 heads.
Use Protect from Missiles to take no damage if ranging, or Protect from Melee to take no damage if meleeing (if low level).
Talk to Tolna.
Talk to him again on the surface.
'Congratulations, quest complete!'
'Note:' Re-enter the rift once you've completed the quest to complete a task from the Varrock Medium Achievement Diary.

name: Rag and Bone Man I
start: Speak to the Odd Old Man, located at the end of the northern path in central Silvarea.
description: Everybody needs some body, and the Odd Old Man knows exactly which bits of those bodies he needs. Can you help him finish his extensive and extremely creepy collection?
itemRequirements: 8 coins for 8 pots of vinegar (bring 68 coins if walking to and from Karamja for boat fare)
8 logs of any type (or an axe to obtain them)
recommendedItems: Combat 15
Teleport runes or tablets to Varrock and Lumbridge
Digsite pendant or Digsite teleport for quick access to the Odd Old Man's house
Amulet of glory for quick access to Draynor Village and Karamja
Dramen staff for Fairy Ring teleports
Access to the Balloon transport system and Willow logs to use it
requiredFor: Rag and Bone Man II - Rag and Bone Man II starts immediately after completing Rag and Bone Man I. The player may begin collecting bones throughout their journey rather than actively seeking each enemy, saving some time down the line.
leagueRegion: <poem> Not completable, as it requires access to Misthalin. </poem>

walkthrough.heading: Starting out
walkthrough.body: Varrock teleport]] or digsite pendant (or usage of the balloon transport system (with willow logs)) for a faster route of travel to the Odd Old Man The Odd Old Man (quest start location) is found east of Varrock and west of Paterdomus Temple in Silvarea. If travelling from Varrock, walk east of the city and through the gate near the Earth Altar, directly east of the nearby statue of Saradomin. If travelling from the Digsite, walk north and east around the mountain. You can also use the balloon Transport System, as one of the destinations is directly north-west of the gate (it is suggested to have the Castle Wars location unlocked due to its proximity to a balloon. Use the minigame teleport to Castle Wars, then fly to the Varrock balloon location (1 willow log required). The Odd Old Man is a fairly short distance to the east). Reaching him will take you down the same path as travelling Canifis would. Halfway down that path, you will find the Odd Old Man to the north, just slightly north-west of the limestone quarry (marked by a quest icon on your minimap, right next to the mining site icon). Talk to him, and he will tell you that he needs several bones to complete his collection. 'Then talk to him again' after getting the list to have him list every bone individually; go through the chat dialogue, where he tells you what bones you have remaining and where to get them individually, until he guides you on how to polish the bones in vinegar. 'If you do not speak to him and go through the entire dialogue, you will be unable to add bones to the pots of vinegar later on unless you talk to him, so doing this will efficiently save you a trip or two.'

walkthrough.heading: Collecting the bones
walkthrough.body: Below is the list of monsters that need to be killed to obtain all the bones (8 total). 'Note:' All of these monsters can be found in other places; listed are the most convenient spots. 'Note:' At any point, a player can turn in a bone or bones to the Odd Old Man, assuming it has been polished. Having all 8 at once is not necessary, but preferable to save time. {|class="wikitable lighttable" style="text-align:center;"!colspan=2|Bone!Monster!Locations (preferable) - Click to mark |- | |Giant rat bone |Giant rat |South-east of Varrock by the mine, Varrock Sewer, Lumbridge Swamp, near the Port Sarim jail. |- | |Unicorn bone |Unicorn |The forest south-east of Varrock, Lumbridge Swamp, by Draynor Village, south of Edgeville, west of Catherby, on Entrana (west from the Law Altar), next to fairy ring BIS in Ardougne Zoo, outside of Corporeal beast cave in Wilderness (very close to Games necklace teleport), Hosidius saltpetre mines (close to the Tithe Farm minigame teleport and Hosidius house portal). |- | |Bear ribs |Bear |The forest south-east of Varrock, the enclosure north-east of the palace in Varrock, north of Falador, the forests near Ardougne (south-west of fairy ring BLR). |- | |Ram skull |Ram |The sheep pen south of Varrock, in Fred the Farmer's sheep pen (north of Lumbridge), north of the Crafting Guild (by the Make-over mage), in the Fisher Realm (fairy ring BJR) after finding Sir Percival. |- | |Goblin skull |Goblin |Both east and west of Lumbridge (the goblins at the farm south of Varrock and north of Ardougne 'do not' drop the bone). |- | |Big frog leg |Big frog |The Lumbridge Swamp. Both the Level 10 and 24 Big Frogs can be killed to acquire the bone. |- | |Monkey paw |Monkey |East of the Karamja Volcano, south Karamja (right next to fairy ring CKR), Ardougne Zoo (if you choose to go to Ardougne Zoo, you must bring ranged and/or magic equipment and have 33 Magic for Telekinetic Grab). |- | |Giant bat wing |Giant bat |Crandor and Karamja Dungeon (which can be accessed on the Karamja Volcano), outside Keep Le Faye (north of fairy ring BLR), below the Heroes' Guild, Yanille dungeon, coal trucks west of McGrubor's Wood, mine west of Tithe Farm (close to the minigame teleport, or Hosidius house portal). |} 8 Coins gp to buy the 8 Jug of vinegar jugs of vinegar with, 60 gp to travel to and back from Karamja (if walking), and 8 empty inventory slots for the bones Collecting all of the required bones is a relatively easy task if you walk south of the Odd Old Man's location, down to Lumbridge, and then to Port Sarim in the west to get to Karamja. Using teleports to get to the required locations will speed up the process (Lumbridge, Draynor Village, and Karamja teleport). Ensure you 'talk to the Odd Old Man before you begin gathering and go through the entire dialogue'. All needed bones are a guaranteed drop.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1108655941006835713|date=21 March 2019|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/97648|archivedate=18 May 2019|quote=The initial quest ones are guaranteed drops. The longer wish-list is 1/4.}} The following is a recommended route for the first six of the eight required bones, starting from the Odd Old Man's house and ending in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. #Run west from the Odd Old Man's house and through the gate, then south to the mines south-east of Varrock and kill a Giant rat near or inside the mine, picking up the giant rat bone it drops in the process. #Head slightly south of the mine to the forest and kill a unicorn and black bear, picking up the unicorn bone and the bear ribs respectively. #Head into the sheep pen to the south-west of the mine and west of the forest and kill a ram to get a ram skull. #Walk south towards Lumbridge (or teleport to the city and walk east) and kill a goblin on the eastern side of the River Lum to get a goblin skull. #Head down to the Lumbridge Swamp and kill one of the big frogs for the big frog leg. The small frogs and giant frogs do 'NOT' drop the big frog leg. From here, head to Draynor Village, north-west of the Lumbridge Swamps. Find and 'talk to' Fortunato in the market about vinegar. Only after talking about vinegar will he have it stocked in the store, trade him and purchase 8 (or 35 if intending to do Rag and Bone Man II at some point, saving time later) jugs of vinegar. '''Do not steal from the market stall or he won't talk to you.' This is also a good opportunity to withdraw items to return to the Odd Old Man (Varrock teleportation runes or tablet, Digsite pendant), and, if returning directly to him, all 6 currently collected bones and the necessary supplies to polish all 8 (8 jugs of vinegar, 8 pots (highly recommended to make the 6 bone in vinegar you currently can and 2 pots of vinegar to save space - see "Polishing the bones" for details), and 8 logs (of any type - alternatively, an axe to cut down the trees by the Odd Old Man, which will save a lot of space)). 'Note:' Be careful that you 'do not' accidentally "empty" a bone in vinegar, because if you do, 'you will lose the bone and have to collect that bone again'''. From here, travel south-west to Port Sarim and take the ship (the third transportation icon from the north, fourth from the south) (requires 30 gp each way) to Karamja (can also teleport (amulet of glory)). Once there: #Walk west towards the Karamja Volcano and kill a monkey on the way, picking up the monkey paw. #Head into the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon, which is located at the top of the Karamja Volcano (marked by a dungeon icon), and kill a giant bat, picking up the giant bat wing. After you've gathered all 8 bones, head back to the Odd Old Man, and a bank if necessary.

walkthrough.heading: Polishing the bones
walkthrough.body: {{Inventory|align=right |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Bone in vinegar |Logs |Logs |Logs |Logs |Logs |Logs |Logs |Logs |Tinderbox |Varrock teleport (tablet) }} 8 bone in vinegar (requiring 8 Jug of vinegar jugs of vinegar, 8 pots, and all 8 bones to make), a tinderbox, 8 logs (of any type - can also bring an axe to chop them down by the Odd Old Man An example of how an inventory looks, before heading back to the Odd Old Man, can be seen on the right. If you haven't already, make 8 pots of vinegar by using the jugs of vinegar on your pots and then use all the bones on the pots of vinegar to make 8 bone in vinegar. 'Note:' Be careful that you 'do not' accidentally "empty" a bone in vinegar, because if you do, 'you will lose the bone and have to collect that bone again'. Go back to the old man taking the eight bones in vinegar, a tinderbox and eight logs (or, alternatively, bring an axe instead of logs; there are trees near the Odd Old Man at the bottom of the stairs where logs can be cut). 'Any' type of logs works for this quest, provided you have the Firemaking level to light the logs. To polish the bones, use a log on the pot-boiler next to the Odd Old Man. Then, use a bone in vinegar on the pot boiler, and finally, use your tinderbox to light it (you will not receive experience for lighting the logs). It takes 12 seconds for each pot to boil. You can hop worlds after lighting the logs to skip these 12 seconds. Repeat this for all eight bones. Talk to the Odd Old Man, and give him the polished bones to complete the quest. 'Congratulations, quest complete!'

steps: Talk to the Odd Old Man in Silvarea, north-east of Varrock, north of the Digsite, during the conversation he will mention boiling the bones in vinegar..
Talk to Fortunato located in Draynor marketplace and buy 8 jug of vinegar.
Use all of the jugs of vinegar with all the pots to make 8 pots of vinegar. If intending to do Rag and Bone Man II, buy 27 more (35 total) jugs of vinegar to save time.
Use all of the bones with your pots of vinegar to get 8 bones in vinegar.
Withdraw a tinderbox and either 8 logs or an axe
With the logs in your inventory, return to the Odd Old Man
For each bone in vinegar do:
Place a set of logs on the pot-boiler next to the old man.
Use a bone in vinegar with the pot-boiler.
Light the set of logs with your tinderbox.
Wait 12 seconds until the fire is consumed and remove the pot from the pot-boiler. (Alternatively, hop worlds after lighting the logs for them to be finished when you log back in)
Talk to the Odd Old Man.
'Congratulations, quest complete!'

name: Swan Song
start: The Piscatoris Fishing Colony. It can be reached via a boat trip from the river to the west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
description: Out on the edge of the known world, the Piscatoris Fishing Colony stands on the brink of disaster. Angry sea trolls are emerging from the sea and attacking the colonists, preventing them from harvesting the valuable monkfish that live in those waters. A highly experienced adventurer will be needed to drive back the trolls for good. The Colony's director, Herman Caranos, has a particular adventurer in mind: the notoriously amoral Wise Old Man of Draynor Village (allegations of his involvement in a spectacular bank robbery have never been substantiated). If you're in the mood for a bit of combat, jump on the boat on the west side of the Gnome Stronghold, speak to the Colony's director and prepare to fight alongside the Wise Old Man as he embarks on his final adventure - his swan song.
itemRequirements: An airtight pot – created by using a pot lid on a pot
Soft clay if making your own pot lid during the quest (2 if also making the pot), or a pickaxe to obtain the clay during the quest
a pickaxe (obtainable during the quest) if mining your own iron during quest
1 set of logs of any kind, or
an axe (obtainable during quest) if chopping your own logs during quest
A small fishing net (obtained during the quest)
A brown apron (obtained during the quest)
recommendedItems: Combat 60
Teleportation method to the Piscatoris Fishing Colony:
Several Piscatoris teleports can be used to teleport there directly
A Dramen staff or Lunar staff – if using fairy rings AKQ
50 coins or a ring of charos – if using Kathy Corkat's boat from west of Tree Gnome Stronghold
An amulet of glory (to teleport to Draynor Village)
A skills necklace (to teleport to the Crafting Guild)
Watchtower teleport runes or tablet (requires completing Watchtower), or Nightmare Zone Minigame Teleport
It is best to bring 4 to 5 Admiral pies if boosting Fishing level.
Some prayer potions (to offset the Sea Troll Queen's magical Prayer-draining attacks)
Some good food/healing
Cooking gauntlets (to reduce the chance of burning the 5 Monkfish caught during the quest)
requirements: The ability to defeat a combat level 170 monster, which is able to use Magic, Melee and can drain Prayer.
enemiesToDefeat: 11 Sea trolls (1 each of levels 65/87/101 and 8 of level 79)
rewards: Access to the Piscatoris Fishing Colony
The ability to use Skeleton Mages for training
Use Kathy Corkat's boat for free
Access to the following items from Malignius Mortifer upon request:
ironmanConcerns: Consider purchasing the necessary combination runes from the Rewards Guardian in the Mage Training Arena.
leagueRegion: <poem> Unlocking Desert will auto-complete the quest Unlocking Fremennik will auto-complete the quest Unlocking Kandarin will auto-complete the quest </poem>

walkthrough.heading: Starting the quest
walkthrough.body: teleport]] to Draynor Village or nearby. The easiest way to reach the Piscatoris Fishing Colony is to teleport using the Piscatoris teleport scroll. It can also be reached by boat, from the river west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold. To use the boat, you must either pay Kathy Corkat 50 coins, or charm her while wearing the Ring of Charos. After you have started the quest, you will not need to pay her again. You can also use the fairy ring code AKQ, and run north-east to the Colony. Once you reach the Colony, walk a short distance north-east, and speak to Herman Caranos. When you agree to help him, the quest will start. He will ask you to find the Wise Old Man of Draynor Village and secure his services. Agree to this, and travel to Draynor Village. <gallery> Swan Song flashback (1).png|Killing an Ogre shaman Swan Song flashback (2).png|Killing the Drunken Dwarf Swan Song flashback (3).png|Subduing The Shaikahan Swan Song flashback (4).png|Fighting the Kalphite Queen Swan Song flashback (5).png|Fighting Dad </gallery>

walkthrough.heading: The Wise Old Man
walkthrough.body: 10 lava runes, 10 mist runes, and 5 blood runes. Talk to the Wise Old Man. After some conversation, he will tell you that he requires 10 lava runes, 10 mist runes, and 5 blood runes before he will help you. Give him these runes and return to the Fishing Colony.

walkthrough.heading: Battle at the Colony
walkthrough.body: Combat equipment to fight 8 level 79 Sea trolls with no Ranged/Magic safespots. teleport]] to Yanille, 5 iron bars, logs, a hammer, and a tinderbox. Fishing level boosting item if you're below 62. {{Instance}} Travel back to the Piscatoris Fishing Colony. The Wise Old Man will be waiting in place of Herman Caranos. Talk to him to enter the main Colony grounds, where you will be attacked by eight (8) level 79 Sea trolls. The Wise Old Man will help you by casting Saradomin Strike on the trolls (he hits super high, sometimes over 40); however, after 10 casts, he runs out of runes and resorts to throwing stones at the trolls, with a maximum hit of 2. Note that you can "use" blood, air, and fire runes on The Wise Old Man during the fight to give him more runes. However, he will only take one rune each time you use them on him, making this not recommended as the trolls will continue to attack you. The trolls only attack with melee so using Protect from Melee will prevent you from taking any damage. Once you have killed the trolls, enter the gates of the Colony. The Wise Old Man will tell you to find Herman Caranos, after which he will disappear. Herman is in the building at the eastern end of the Colony. :'Tip': Pick up the bones that the trolls drop as you'll need 7 of them later in the quest. :'Optional:' You can search Herman's desk for a book, which tells you about the Wise Old Man's past. If you have a house with a bookcase in it, this book will become available after the quest. When you talk to Herman, the Wise Old Man will reappear. You will then be told to do some odd jobs around the colony.

walkthrough.heading: Repairing the Colony
walkthrough.body: The following two tasks can be done in any order: #Talk with Arnold Lydspor, and refill the Fishing Colony's food stocks. #Talk with Franklin Caranos, and repair the Colony's walls. ====Arnold Lydspor==== Arnold Lydspor can be located in the bank to the west of Herman Caranos, at the bank sign on the minimap. :'Note:' Arnold's bank and general store cannot be accessed until the quest is complete. He will tell you that the Fishing Colony has no food and that he needs five cooked fresh monkfish. He will give you a small fishing net with which to catch fresh monkfish. The fishing spot for them is located to the north-west. If you are using a boost to exactly level 62, bring at least eight doses because trolls will spawn each time you try to fish, which will take up time and your level may drop. Catch a few extra as you may burn the fish. While fishing, you will be attacked by three Sea Trolls whose levels get progressively higher - levels 65, 87 and 101. You must kill these in order to continue fishing. When you have caught the fresh monkfish, you can cook it on a range to the south. When you have five cooked fresh monkfish, take them to Arnold. If you burn some, you can give him the cooked ones and go back to fish for more. Despite being quest items, once cooked the left-click of fresh monkfish is "eat", and they will heal 1hp if eaten. ====Franklin Caranos==== Franklin Caranos is near the entrance gate of the Colony. He will ask you to make five iron sheets to repair the west walls. He will give you a tinderbox to heat the metal press. If you have the iron bars and logs, you can skip the following steps: Pick up a pickaxe and an axe from the pile east of Franklin. Exit the Colony via the gate, and head back underneath the hole. To the south, you should find several rocks; mine enough iron ores to make five iron bars (you will be able to smith them with the usual 50% success rate at the Colony), and cut down a dead tree for some logs. Return to the Colony and smith your ores into bars, returning to the rocks and mining more ores if required, until you have five bars. Go into the building with the furnace, and use your logs on the Firebox east end of the press then use the tinderbox and light them. Then, use your iron bars with the press to make iron sheets. Tell Franklin that you have the sheets and he will give you a hammer, with which you can repair the walls to the west. Once you have done this, talk to Franklin again. Note: When you repair the wall, you need to use the iron sheets on the broken wall. If you use the hammer on the broken wall, your character will yell and hammer the wall. You'll receive a message that you feel a lot calmer, but it didn't achieve anything, and to use the iron sheets on the wall instead. 'Important:' Keep the pickaxe since you'll need it to mine clay in the next part if you didn't bring any.

walkthrough.heading: Raising an army
walkthrough.body: A pickaxe (to mine the clay, needed only if you didn't bring any). Next, go back to the Wise Old Man and Herman Caranos, who tell you that they need an army to fight and defeat the Sea trolls once and for all. The Wise Old Man tells you to visit Wizard Frumscone, in the basement of the Wizards' Guild. :'Note:' This is where you need to boost your Magic level if it is lower than 66. You may find it advisable to pick up a pickaxe, if you have not done so already, before you leave for Yanille. You can use any recommended methods as mentioned to travel to Yanille. If you use the minigame teleport to the Nightmare Zone you will need to leave the area through the tunnel first. At Yanille, you may get seven normal bones, pot, and pot lid from the bank if you have them. Head into the Wizards' Guild and go down the ladder. Wizard Frumscone will appear and refuse to help you, but he does tell you of one who may - Malignius Mortifer. 'Important:' Be sure to bank any Saradomin-related items prior to talking to Malignius, or he will refuse to help you. The Saradomin Cape does not count. As he teleports you to Piscatoris Fishing Colony when you speak to him, it is not advised to drop any items. After making the pottery, however, you may wear your items. {{Map|name=Malignius Mortifer|x=2990|y=3268|r=10|mtype=square|width=250|height=250|align=right|caption=Malignius Mortifer's location.}} You can use your charged amulet of glory if you have them to teleport to Draynor Village, and head west to find Malignius, who is accompanied by elemental wizards, slightly north-west of the Port Sarim magic shop. Alternatively, you can use the southern portal at the top of the Guild to take you to the Dark Wizards' Tower. The dark wizards drop bones, so you can kill seven of them for seven bones if you still need them. Walk south, through the gate, and then south-east from here to find Malignius. Malignius will tell you that he needs seven normal bones. You can kill highwaymen or the chickens in the farm nearby for these. (You cannot kill the surrounding wizards, as they drop ashes.) When you give them to him, he will tell you that you also need some way of storing the seeds he will give you, and that you should ask in the Crafting Guild to the west. He will give you a brown apron, which will allow you access. Ask the master craftsmen (the one with no skillcape) about how to store the seeds until you find the one that will tell you; you will need simply a pot with a pot lid. You may skip the rest of this paragraph if you have both items. Mine two pieces of clay in the Guild mine; use the jug in the northern end of the Guild filled with water from the sink to the south to soften the clay, and then shape them on the potter's wheel. Fire them in the pottery oven. :'Warning:' Now, you may wish to restock your combat supplies for the upcoming fight at a bank as Malignius will, without any warning, teleport you to the Piscatoris Fishing Colony after you have finished talking with him. Now, return to Malignius with your pot and pot lid, and he will teleport you to the Fishing Colony.

walkthrough.heading: The final battle
walkthrough.body: Bone seeds, Combat equipment to defeat a level 170 Sea Troll Queen, which is able to use Magic and Melee and can drain Prayer. Ranged/Magic safespots are available but not advisable. {{Instance}} After entering the Colony and talking to Herman Caranos, you will be shown a cutscene of your army of Skeleton Mages defeating the Sea trolls and then the Wise Old Man killing the levelless Sea Troll General. However, while he is celebrating, he gets hit for 254 damage (which doesn't make the slightest dent on his health bar). He will be disabled for the rest of the fight, so you must take on the Sea Troll Queen yourself. <gallery> Rise from the Sea.png|The Sea Trolls rise from the ocean depths. Swan Song army.png|This means war! Sea Troll General dies.png|The Wise Old Man kills the Sea Troll General Wise Old Man weakened.png|The Wise Old Man is badly hurt by a powerful water spell. The Sea Troll Queen.png|You must fight the Sea Troll Queen! </gallery> The Queen cannot move from her location, so anywhere not directly next to her is suitable for long-ranged attacks. The Queen uses the Magic attack Water Wave and a basic Melee attack where possible. If you are using overhead protection prayers and are not within melee range, the queen will use a Prayer-draining attack. This means that long-ranged attacks are inadvisable unless you are confident in your armour to protect you from powerful magical spells (e.g. Armadyl armour). Meleeing the queen means she will not use her prayer draining attack; however, she uses both Melee and Magic attacks. She is much more damaging with magical attacks, with a max hit of '37', so it is 'best to use Protect from Magic and wear melee armour'. She is not too hard for a skilled fighter, though she should not be taken for a pushover either, as her melee can still hit up to 16. It is possible to wear full Mystic robes and use the Mystic Might Prayer. This way the queen splashes more often. Be careful though, she can still hit 25 consistently. Use the best Wave spell you can. After defeating the queen, talk to Herman to finish the quest. 'Congratulations, quest complete!'

update: Return of the Wise Old Man!

steps: Talk to Herman Caranos at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony (north of Fairy ring AKQ); cutscene is optional.
Talk to the Wise Old Man in Draynor Village.
Return to the Colony and talk to the Wise Old Man.
Kill the level 79 Sea Trolls and enter the Colony (collect 7 of their bones if needed).

Talk to Herman (east building). '''Note:' You will need to click inside of the building as clicking directly on Herman (or the Wise Old Man later) will make your character run outside the building to the north.''
Talk to Franklin Caranos near the entrance.
Use a log on the firebox (not the furnace) and light it in the building with the Furnace symbol. (Franklin will give you a tinderbox if you speak to him again.)
Use each of the five iron bars on the Metal Press.
Use iron sheets to repair the western colony perimeter's broken walls. (Franklin will give you a hammer.)
Talk to Arnold Lydspor in the bank. (He will give you a Small fishing net if you do not already have one.)
Fish 5 fresh monkfish at the fishing spot to the north-west, you may need a few more if you burn some while cooking.
Kill sea trolls when they spawn, as they will increase in difficulty. After 1-3 kills, the sea trolls only drop big bones and cannot be used in the next section of the quest.
Cook the monkfish in the kitchen, south of the fishing spot. Note: you cannot bank with Arnold to make use of cooking gauntlets.
Talk to Arnold.
Talk to Franklin.
Talk to the Wise Old Man and Herman in the far eastern building.
Talk to Wizard Frumscone in the basement of the Wizards' Guild in Yanille.
Talk to Malignius Mortifer south of Falador. He will give you a brown apron in order to be allowed entry to the Crafting Guild.
Talk to the Master Crafter with dreadlocks in the Crafting Guild on the east side.
If you brought soft clay, use it on the potter's wheel, then the potter's oven to make a pot and pot lid. If you brought a pickaxe, mine some clay and follow the step above.
Use Pot and Pot Lid together to make Airtight Pot.
Talk to Malignius Mortifer to teleport back to the Fishing Colony.
Talk to Herman to begin the fight.
Kill the Sea Troll Queen. (Use Protect from Magic in Melee range, and use Ranged or Melee to kill her)
Talk to Herman.
'Congratulations, quest complete!'
(Optional) Catch and cook a monkfish to complete a hard Western Provinces Achievement Diary task.

name: Royal Trouble
start: Go to Miscellania and speak to Advisor Ghrim in the castle.
description: It's tough being a regent of a small island kingdom, especially when the king has declared war while you were adventuring. Something is up in Miscellania and Etceteria, so you'd better find out what before both kingdoms end up in royal trouble.
itemRequirements: 5 coal (obtainable during the quest with a pickaxe, which will also be obtainable)
recommendedItems: Combat 50
Weapon, armour and some food
Superantipoison or any other poison cure
Prayer 43 and Prayer potions for protection prayers
Stamina or energy potions
Multiple charged Rings of Wealth for fast travel to Miscellania
rewards: The ability to hire Bosun Zarah as a crewmate with Sailing 80
leagueRegion: <poem> Fremennik — location requirement </poem>

walkthrough.heading: Stolen goods
walkthrough.body: Speak to the King. He'll say that several items from many of Miscellania's citizens have been going missing, and that you should investigate. Find and speak with either Gunnhild by the herbs, Leif by the trees, Frodi on the dock, or Magnus by the mines (they will all say the same thing, you only need to talk to one of them). Apparently, Etceterian soldiers came to ask for tithes, the workers refused, and the next day items were stolen. Talk with the King again. He'll send you to discuss this situation with Queen Sigrid.

walkthrough.heading: More stolen goods
walkthrough.body: Speak with Queen Sigrid in Etceteria. She'll tell you to talk to her citizens about things gone missing, criticising the king whenever she gets the chance. Go downstairs to speak to one of the Etceterian citizens such as Helga, Haming, or Matilda. They will tell you the same story as the workers in Miscellania, only with the roles reversed. Speak again with Queen Sigrid and update her on the known information. Soldiers have been mentioned in both stories, yet neither side has an army. She'll say this is your responsibility due to your position as regent and demand you solve things. '''Note:' Be sure to have the things you will need for the fight at this point, utilising the bank directly north on Etceteria. Remember to take antipoison potions and prayer potions as needed. It is recommended to leave about 10 inventory spaces open for items you're going to use later on during the quest.''

walkthrough.heading: To the dungeon with you!
walkthrough.body: Go back to Miscellania and speak with King Vargas to review your conversation with the Queen. He'll ask you to speak with Ghrim about the presence of these alleged armies and the missing goods. Ghrim, assuming these happenings are being caused by outsiders, will suggest you speak with the Sailor at the docks to find out if he's seen any suspicious characters. Head to the Sailor at the docks of Miscellania. He will mention a group of children who came to the island recently, saying they had gone to go visit their family in the dungeon. The dungeon is still inaccessible at this point, so speak again with King Vargas to gain access. He'll give you a scroll with his signature. Take the scroll and enter the dungeon within Miscellania's castle walls (look for the dungeon icon on the minimap), and you will arrive in a small underground settlement. Go to the pub and speak with a dwarf called Donal.

walkthrough.heading: Repairing the lift
walkthrough.body: 9 free inventory spaces, 5 coal (or you can mine the coal from the chamber with a pickaxe you can find near the dwarf miners) Upon speaking with Donal, he'll talk about a monster deep within the caves. He'll give you a mining prop to get through the passage and into a room with a broken lift. Head up north, and you will see two dwarf miners. Pick up a bronze pickaxe from the rock if you need one. Use the mining prop on the crevice and squeeze through it. Now, you need to repair the lift using items found in the boxes in the chamber: #First, take an engine and three beams, three pulley beams, and two ropes from the crates. #Before you start assembling the whole structure, add five chunks of coal to the engine (this can also be done last, after step 8). If you did not bring coal with you, the chamber has four coal rocks as well as a pickaxe near the dwarves if you forgot one. #Use a pulley beam on the broken scaffold on the east side of the room to attach it. #Use a beam on a pulley beam to make a long pulley beam, and then use it with another beam to get a longer pulley beam, which you must then attach to the scaffold. #Use the final pulley beam on the scaffold. #Use a rope on the scaffold to wind it through the pulleys. #Use the third beam on the platform to repair it. #Place the engine on the engine platform (Note: the engine platform is not the same as the platform from step 7. Rather, it is the one on the tile which faces the engine spawning spot). #Add the 5 pieces of coal to the engine (only necessary if not already added). The lift should be operational now. While making sure you have another rope, click the 'Use-Lift' option on the platform to head closer to the mysteries of the island. ''(If this option doesn't appear, make sure you have added 5 coal to the engine. You can do it when placed on the engine platform.)''

walkthrough.heading: The burnt diary
walkthrough.body: Take the plank and enter the small tunnel on the east wall. Continue travelling east and use a rope with the overhanging rock to swing across the water. You will come across the remains of a fire, search it to get the first part of a burnt diary. Read the diary, and save it for later. Use the plank to cross the slippery rocks - otherwise, you may be hit for 8 damage. The plank is not left behind and may be reused every time. The rocks can also be safely skipped without a plank via the run trick. As you proceed further into the caves, you will come across two more fire remains, search them to get the second and third part of the diary. After the third fire remains, there will be some steam vents in the ground. 'Do not walk across or stand on them as they repeatedly damage you depending on your Hitpoints level.' After the vents, there will be another set of fire remains, search it for the fourth part of the diary. Going further down into the caves, there will be some rocks lying on the cliffs above your path. 'Do not stand or walk under those rocks as they will fall down on you and deal some damage depending on your Hitpoints level.' After progressing through the area with the rocks, you will come across yet another fire remains. Search it to find the fifth and final page for the diary. Once you have completed the diary, you must read it before being able to enter a crevice at the end of the passage.

walkthrough.heading: Those meddling kids!
walkthrough.body: Enter through the crevice, and you should see a cutscene involving some lost kids. Speak to them to get the full story. The kids had apparently not been able to pass the trials to become a Fremennik, so they were going to start a war here and then stop it, and be seen as heroes. They are to blame for everything. Travel out through the next exit, and roam the passages where there are lots of Sea Snake Young until you reach another crevice; squeeze through and kill the Giant Sea Snake (level 149, with only 100 HP).

walkthrough.heading: King of Slither and Thither
walkthrough.body: {{Instance}} Protect from Melee works fine if you want to run up close. From a distance the snake uses ranged attacks so use Protect from Missiles if ranging or maging. Level 60 Magic and Iban blast will be enough to kill the snake quickly. A Dwarf multicannon can be setup in the boss room to help lower levels defeat the Giant Sea Snake. Its poison damage hits 9 so an antipoison is 'strongly' recommended. Note that a superantipoison will also negate any effects for 5 minutes. A player who has around level 70 Ranged, full Black d'hide, a Magic Shortbow (i), and Rune arrows, for example, should only need 1 dose of normal Antipoison to kill the Snake. Similarly, level ~70 Melee stats with a Dragon scimitar should also only need 1 dose of antipoison. After the fight, it is also recommended to immediately drink your antipoison because the damage of the poison is very slow, yet heavy.

walkthrough.heading: At peace once again
walkthrough.body: Pick up the heavy box that the snake drops. If you forget to collect the box before leaving, speak to the guard outside the dungeon on Etceteria. Return through the crevice. A guard will notice you and help you up, and you will surface near Sigrid's castle. Go to Queen Sigrid and talk to her. She'll be impressed with you, and she'll give you 20,000 coins as a reward and a letter to take to King Vargas (reading it will not affect the quest). Talk to King Vargas to give him the letter for the rest of your reward. 'Congratulations, quest complete!'

steps: Speak to Advisor Ghrim. (fairy ring code cip)
Talk to Princess Astrid or Prince Brand (depending on who you married), watch the cutscene.
Talk to King Vargas.
Talk to Gardener Gunnhild by the flax patch next to the castle entrance.
Talk to Queen Sigrid.
Talk to Matilda in/around the southern building inside the castle's walls.
Talk to Queen Sigrid.

Now is a good time to gear up at the bank at the north part of Etceteria as you won't be coming back here until after the boss fight. Don't forget to take an antipoison to help with the fight. Also take 5 coal or have at least 5 empty spaces. Note: Do not waste time trying to mine coal near Miner Magnus, as you don't actually get any resources. An area to mine coal is provided later on in the quest.
Talk to King Vargas.
Talk to Advisor Ghrim.
Talk to the Sailor at the Miscellania docks.
Talk to King Vargas with one open inventory slot to receive a scroll proving you are Regent of Miscellania.
Enter the dungeon, down the ladder in the courtyard (along the castle's south wall).
Talk to Donal in the pub.
Go north, take a pick (on the rock next to the dwarves) if you need coal.
Use the mining prop on the crevice and proceed through the crevice.
Take an engine and put the 5 coal in it.
Take the following from the crates:
2 beams.
3 pulley beams.
1 rope.
Use a beam on a pulley beam to get a long pulley beam; use another regular beam on it to make a longer pulley beam.
To the 'broken scaffold' add:
A pulley beam.
A longer pulley beam.
A pulley beam.
A rope.
Take:
1 beam.
1 rope.
Add a beam to the 'platform'.
Put the engine on the 'engine platform'.
If you haven't yet, add your five coal to the engine.
Use the lift and take the plank.
Enter the tunnel, run east, and use your rope on the rock.
Keep running and make sure to continue through your character's dialogue.
Take the diary from the fire remains.
Use your plank to cross the rocks, be sure to 'collect all diary pages by searching the four additional fires through the cave'.
Continue running and avoid the steam vents as they will damage you.
Read the diary and continue through the crevice, watch the cutscene.
Talk to Armod.
Follow the passage north and enter the crevice at the end of the passage
Kill the Giant Sea Snake. Use protect from ranged prayer and attack at a distance (magic preferred).
Take the heavy box.
Leave the crevice of the boss room and climb up the rope for a shortcut back to Etceteria castle.
Talk to Queen Sigrid to receive a letter and 20000 gold. (You need two free inventory slots.)
Talk to King Vargas.

name: Death to the Dorgeshuun
start: Speak to Mistag in the Dorgesh-Kaan mine.
description: Humans have been visiting the Dorgeshuun mines for some time now, but no Dorgeshuun has visited the surface since the signing of the Lumbridge-Dorgeshuun treaty. The Dorgeshuun Council fears that the H.A.M. group may be planning another attack, and want to send an agent to the surface to investigate. But they do not want to send someone to the surface without a guide...
itemRequirements: Any light source (lanterns are recommended - open light sources such as a candle can cause gas explosions and require a tinderbox)

2 full sets of H.A.M. robes (all 7 pieces) (chance to receive robes is significantly higher during the quest){{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1112039679547850752|date=30 March 2018|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/109636|archivedate=28 May 2020|quote=Are you on the bit of the quest where you need it? If so, the chance of you getting HAM kit is considerably higher.}}
Pickaxe (if not using a games necklace to teleport to Tears of Guthix - only usable after you have completed the Tears of Guthix quest)
recommendedItems: Combat 30
Weapon, armour, and some food
Games necklace to Tears of Guthix (only usable after you have completed the Tears of Guthix quest)
Lumbridge teleport runes or teleportation tabs
A lit sapphire lantern.
Chisel
Pickaxe
Rope (if using the Lumbridge Swamp entrance for the first time)
requirements: The ability to defeat a level 50 enemy with Melee or Magic
rewards: Access to the H.A.M. Store room, where you can loot gems, jewellery, and coins from chests
Access to the water wheel tunnel (Dartog will appear there, and you'll be able to travel between the Lumbridge Castle cellar, the Dorgeshuun Mines and the water wheel tunnel at will)
Ability to use the bone dagger and Dorgeshuun crossbow special attacks
Access to Dorgesh-Kaan, the Dorgeshuun city
A torch if you did not have a light source in your inventory at the end of the quest
leagueRegion: <poem> Not completable, as it requires access to Misthalin. </poem>

walkthrough.heading: Infiltrating the H.A.M. hideout
walkthrough.body:
